patients with postoperative IMRCT with R0- 1 status reach significantly higher loco-regional and overall disease control rates than patients following definitive IMRT for macroscopically visible disease.
IMRT in OCC patients with R0-0 status (i.e. no gross disease) is superior to patients treated for macroscopic tumor, in terms of LRC and OSA.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the treatment of patients with oral cavity carcinoma.
the treatment of patients with oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCC) in the era of intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT).

the development of a new generation of radiation therapy techniques, namely intensity-modulated radiation therapy (i.e. IMRT), and the use of new biological agents (e.g. anti-angiogenetic drugs, anti-EGFR drugs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IMRT is a valuable option in the management of OCC, particularly in patients with R0-0 situations.
IMRT is an effective tool for the management of OCC.
IMRT in OCC patients with R0- or R1- status after prior surgery and/or chemo/radiation therapy is associated with excellent LRC and OSA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IMRT is a safe and effective treatment modality for patients with OCC.
IMRT is a valuable option for patients with primary and recurrent OCC, but that it is of utmost importance to achieve an R0-1 situation.
the IMRT era for OCC has begun.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IMRT for R0 resected OCC patients is a highly effective and well tolerated approach, and should be considered standard care in these patients.
IMRT should be considered in the postoperative setting for R0- and R1-occult disease in OCC.
patients with R0-2 status following surgery alone should be considered for adjuvant IMRT, as the risk of loco-regional recurrence in these patients is very high, even after IMRT.
